subject: physics

unit.name: System of Particles and Rotational Motion

chapter: System of Particles and Rotational Motion
question_text: Find the torque of the force 7i + 3j − 5k about the origin. The force acts on a particle whose position vector is i − j + k.

verification.note: Sri Chaitanya IPE Junior Fastrack (Rev. May 2024), Unit 7 VERY SHORT ANSWER (numerical; also NCERT in-text). The 1+1 split — setup, then value — is invented and needs a Telangana IPE teacher. The determinant expansion is hand-checked: τ = (−1·−5 − 1·3)i − (1·−5 − 1·7)j + (1·3 − (−1)·7)k = 2i + 12j + 10k.

recall_prompt: Say the steps you would write for this answer, in order. You can speak in English, in Telugu, or in both.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: The setup
lines: Torque about the origin is the vector

lines.text: τ = r × F,  r = i − j + k,

steps.margin_note: Write τ = r × F and the two vectors before touching the determinant.
steps.why: The cross product is the whole physics here; the determinant is only the bookkeeping for it.
common_mistakes: Computing F × r instead — the cross product changes sign when swapped.

recall.must_convey: That torque is r cross F, with the given r and F written down.
reject: two i plus twelve j plus ten k

steps.memory_tip: Write r on the top row of the determinant and F below. That order decides the sign.

steps.label: The value
lines: Expanding the determinant of the unit
vectors with r and F rows,
steps.margin_note: One line for the expansion, then box the vector. Give the unit.
common_mistakes: Dropping the minus sign that belongs to the j component of the expansion.

recall.must_convey: That the torque works out to 2i + 12j + 10k.
accept: two i plus twelve j plus ten k

steps.memory_tip: Check it: τ·F = 2(7) + 12(3) + 10(−5) = 0. A cross product is perpendicular to both.

insider_note: Only two marks, and the middle term is where they are lost: the j component carries the extra minus sign of the expansion.
